extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for Compositio Mathematica (mathematics researchers submitting to the journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on preparing files and ancillary materials for submission to Compositio Mathematica, including accessibility, labelling, supplementary materials, and optional language-editing services. Focused on the technical/format requirements and responsibilities of authors prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For login and submission support, authors should visit the submission and support pages. Click 'Proceed to submission system' to continue to the partner's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials: status and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials will be published with the same metadata as your parent article, and are considered a formal part of the academic record, so cannot be retracted or modified other than via our article correction processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary materials will not be typeset or copyedited, so should be supplied exactly as they are to appear online. Authors should be familiar with the detailed guidance on supplementary materials prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: English language editing (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, particularly those whose first language is not English, may wish to have their English-language manuscripts checked by a native speaker before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language-editing services are optional and available via Cambridge's language services page. Use of these services is voluntary and at the author's own expense; use does not guarantee acceptance nor restrict submission to Cambridge-published journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requirements (WCAG 2.1 Level AA)
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published by Cambridge are required to meet the accessibility standards outlined in the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should carefully consider elements such as colour use, contrast, and text clarity when preparing images and tables. For detailed guidance on image and multimedia file preparation and preferred formats, see the Cambridge Journals Artwork Guide and Preparing Accessible Materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image, table, and multimedia descriptions (alt-text and accessibility materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility materials must be made available for all figures, tables, and multimedia content to be published within the article, including the provision of image descriptions or 'alt-text' for all figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged, as the subject expert, to prepare their own alt-text and video/audio descriptions and submit them via the Accessibility Descriptions Submission Form. If accessibility materials are required and not provided with the accepted manuscript files, machine-generated descriptions will be created and made available to review at proof stage. The accuracy of accessibility materials is the responsibility of the author; these should be checked carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labelling and citation of illustrative materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All illustrative materials should be referred to in your manuscript text as 'Figures'. Tables and figures must be cited in the text, must be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals, and captions must be provided in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagrams, graphs, maps, boxes, graphical diagrams, and code snippets must also be labelled and numbered. For further information, see Preparing Accessible Materials.
